timeline: If you stood on the dry Rajasthani plains, you would never guess that massive water systems supplied an army of fifty thousand atop Chittor Fort.
Medieval engineers carved eighty-four massive water bodies straight into the rock.
Rainfall filled ponds and deep stepwells to supply fifty thousand defenders for years.
Enemy armies could blockade the gates, yet the summit never ran dry.
Even isolated on a barren precipice, the fortress outlasted every siege.
